Dr. Sweis was great. There is a lot of reading for the class. We read four books in total not including textbook chapters and individual chapters from longer readings. Readings tend to be interesting and easy to understand. 

There are two exams and two short essays (6-8 pages). Exams are easy if you do the readings and come to class.

Dr. Sweis selected interesting readings and I enjoyed the work. When she had her plan, she taught well. However, she was rarely available out of class and her tests and teaching are very methodical and classes often seemed like regurgitations of the reading. While kind and respectful, unfortunately, she often did not bring much energy in class.

The course itself was pretty interesting, but Dr. Sweis can come across as passive-aggressive and very patronizing at times. She's nice, but it's a condescending type of nice. Her grading standards are strict and arbitrary. Don't take this class if you don't care about anthro -- she grades as if it should be your biggest passion.

My fourth class with Dr. Sweis- I would take more. She's absolutely brilliant and truly knows her field. She breaks down material well and facilitates in-depth discussion and analysis. Her content is engaging and relevant, and she challenges students to dig deeper than the surface. She is a supportive mentor in and out of class. I highly recommend.

Dr. Sweis changed my career path through this course. I have never had a professor inspire me through their lectures before. She assigns A LOT of reading, but it is so interesting that you will actually enjoy it.

Prof. Sweis is a really smart medical anthropologist who is excited to share her knowledge and passion with students. Her class is hard, but it opened my mind up to so many things, and now I want to go into medical anthropology myself. She will rock your world a bit, highly recommend for premed students.

This class has had a huge impact on my critical thinking and the trajectory of my academic career. Professor Sweis provided a safe and engaging space to read and talk about the ways in which science is shaped by culture/politics, which is a tough topic, especially considering the range of disciplines the students taking this course came from.

I've had this professor in the past and she's been great, but this semester she could not have been worse. She was not helpful at all, lacked so much clarity, and was barely available for office hours. She is a good teacher and her lectures were interesting, she was not clear about what she expected in our work at all.
She is a tough teacher, especially in her Biopolitics course, but it is all interesting stuff. You have to do the readings and participate in class.
Dr. Sweis was a wonderful professor. She genuinely cared about her students and was thoroughly knowledgeable about the information discussed in class. I would definitely recommend her :)
GREAT PROFESSOR! Books were expensive for her class, but she was so great. Always kept the class interesting and challenging. She's a fair grader.
